title: Align columns with a tab
description: Write a function `table_row(name, age, country, city)` that joins the four values with tab escape sequences between them.
hints: \t inside a string inserts a tab character, which most terminals render as enough spaces to align to the next tab stop - handy for lining up columns without counting spaces.
Build an f-string that places \t between the four values, and return it.
expected_behavior: Returns the four values separated by tab characters.
solution:
def table_row(name, age, country, city):
    return f"{name}\t{age}\t{country}\t{city}"
explanation: \t behaves like \n but inserts a tab instead of a line break - both are single-character escape sequences, not two separate characters.
